metadata.title: The Two 52-Vertex Counterexamples to the Petersen Coloring Conjecture Are Colorable Only by Themselves If No Counterexample Has at Most 38 Vertices
metadata.description:
For cubic graphs G and H, an H-coloring of G maps the edges of G to the edges of H so that every vertex star of G goes bijectively onto a vertex star of H; a Petersen coloring is the case where H is the Petersen graph. The graphs that no bridgeless cubic graph of smaller order colors form the set H_3 of Ma et al., infinite since the conjecture was refuted in 2026. Goedgebeur et al. asked whether their 52-vertex counterexamples are colorable only by themselves.

We prove that the fibers of the vertex map of an H-coloring have the same parity and that unused target vertices reduce to at most one; three kinds of coloring remain, and the question becomes one propositional formula per target order, with the target graph unknown. We prove the formula's symmetry breaking sound and certify each refutation with a DRAT proof checked by drat-trim. For both counterexamples every even target order from 40 to 50 is refuted; for the first one so are 2, 4 and 24 to 38. Assuming the computation of the same authors, that no bridgeless cubic graph on at most 38 vertices lacks a Petersen coloring, both graphs belong to H_3. Without the two lemmas ten orders of the first graph stayed undecided after 35 minutes; with them each took 137 to 5,882 seconds. Orders 6 to 22 of the first graph and 6 to 38 of the second remain undecided; 2 and 4 follow from 3-edge-colorability.

Source code, data, computational records and verification instructions: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/combinatorics/petersen-coloring, computation EXP-007).
metadata.version_notes: Revision of the first version. The method is stated in full: the formula is given as an algorithm with every variable and clause family and its size as a function of the orders of the graph and of the target; the symmetry breaking is proved sound and canonical; the static attach clauses that were part of the certified formulas are listed and proved implied by the others; the certification pipeline is given as an algorithm with its parameters, tool versions and commands. The main theorem is stated as conditional on Observation 10 of arXiv:2608.10028v4, with the dependence in its hypothesis, and a limitations section is added. New tables record the orders without an answer, the 21 control instances, an ablation of the fiber constraints and the SHA-256 of every certified formula and proof; new figures show the three kinds of vertex maps, the formula size, the solve and check times, the proof sizes, the status of every order and the controls. Corrections: the proposition on target order n-2 now assumes a simple graph; the controls are located in the result files with the suffixes red and unred; the orders below 40 of the second 52-vertex graph are stated as not attempted, and the orders 52 to 60 of the 68-vertex graph as stopped, capped or not attempted; the solve times marked n/a are explained (post hoc checks) and the portfolio run is stated; evidence marks are added to every statement; the CaDiCaL reference is qualified; the abstract is shortened to 250 words and the title carries the condition on Observation 10 of arXiv:2608.10028v4 on which membership rests; orders 2 and 4 of every graph are settled by 3-edge-colorability. The computational results of the first version are unchanged.
